![](images/07/078f9509a08715c2a842bc9b8e12bfb3da9b9d77950275174ac684b399d06a68.png)" :question/worked-solution "First, let $P(x,y)=-y$ and $Q(x,y)=0.$

Our simple, smooth, closed path $C$ is positively oriented, and

$$\frac{\partial Q}{\partial x}-\frac{\partial P}{\partial y}=0-(-1)=1.$$

So, according to Green's theorem, we can write the area of the region $D$ enclosed by the curve $C$ as follows:

$$\begin{aligned}\text{Area}(D)&=\iint_D\text{d}A\\&=\iint_D(\frac{\partial Q}{\partial x}-\frac{\partial P}{\partial y})\,\text{d}A\\&=\oint_C P\,\text{d}x+Q\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}$$

Substituting $P(x,y)=-y$ and $Q(x,y)=0,$ we get

$$\oint_C P\,\text{d}x+Q\,\text{d}y=-\oint_C y\,\text{d}x.$$

The derivative of $r(t)$ is

$$r'(t)=\langle -5\sin t,6\cos t\rangle.$$

Therefore, we can write our line integral as

$$\begin{aligned}-\oint_C y\,\text{d}x&=-\int_0^{2\pi}6\sin t\cdot(-5\sin t)\,\text{d}t\\&=30\int_0^{2\pi}\sin^2 t\,\text{d}t\\&=30\int_0^{2\pi}\frac{1-\cos 2t}{2}\,\text{d}t\\&=\int_0^{2\pi}\left(15-15\cos 2t\right)\,\text{d}t\\&=\left[15t-\frac{15}{2}\sin 2t\right]_0^{2\pi}\\&=\left(30 \pi-0\right)-\left(0-0\right)\\&=30 \pi\end{aligned}$$

Therefore, we conclude that $\text{Area}(D)=30 \pi.$" :question/difficulty :question.difficulty/easy :question/answer-fields ["f9fb3ea4-caed-5a83-9c02-6440b3eab456"] :db/ensure :question/validate} {:db/id "f8d8532e-17d1-5493-9f25-92eb498314f2" :answer/id #uuid "f8d8532e-17d1-5493-9f25-92eb498314f2" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "6 \pi" :db/ensure :answer/validate} {:db/id "c8b21cf5-b029-596f-9daa-1704136d990f" :answer/id #uuid "c8b21cf5-b029-596f-9daa-1704136d990f" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "3 \pi" :db/ensure :answer/validate} {:db/id "86844522-ff99-5a89-bd9a-bb2ab32a4d4c" :answer/id #uuid "86844522-ff99-5a89-bd9a-bb2ab32a4d4c" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "36 \pi" :db/ensure :answer/validate} {:db/id "9e5331c0-17c1-57d8-b981-80bc93013514" :answer/id #uuid "9e5331c0-17c1-57d8-b981-80bc93013514" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "- 18 \pi" :db/ensure :answer/validate} {:db/id "f49d5766-20e5-5f10-b5e7-ff819c91de23" :answer/id #uuid "f49d5766-20e5-5f10-b5e7-ff819c91de23" :answer/type :answer.type/math :answer/value "18 \pi" :db/ensure :answer/validate} {:db/id "b6a49ae3-c511-509c-a7e2-5e82cb83cd8f" :answer-field/id #uuid "b6a49ae3-c511-509c-a7e2-5e82cb83cd8f" :answer-field/key "selection" :answer-field/type :answer-field.type/radio :answer-field/choices ["f8d8532e-17d1-5493-9f25-92eb498314f2" "c8b21cf5-b029-596f-9daa-1704136d990f" "86844522-ff99-5a89-bd9a-bb2ab32a4d4c" "9e5331c0-17c1-57d8-b981-80bc93013514" "f49d5766-20e5-5f10-b5e7-ff819c91de23"] :answer-field/correct "f49d5766-20e5-5f10-b5e7-ff819c91de23" :db/ensure :answer-field/validate} {:db/id "e5a8981d-48dd-5bc9-9468-7747b7d1e093" :question/id #uuid "e5a8981d-48dd-5bc9-9468-7747b7d1e093" :question/problem "Use Green's theorem to find the area of the region $D$ enclosed by the curve $C$ parametrized as $r(t)=3\cos t\,i+6\sin t\,j$ for $t\in[0,2\pi].$

$$
\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y}=0-(-1)=1.
$$

So, according to Green's theorem, we can write the area of the region $D$ enclosed by the curve $C$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\text{Area}(D) & ={∬}_{D}\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{∂Q}{∂x}-\frac{∂P}{∂y})\text{d}A \\  & ={∮}_{C}P\,\text{d}x+Q\,\text{d}y\end{aligned}
$$

  

Substituting $P(x,y)=-y$ and $Q(x,y)=0,$ we get

$$
{∮}_{C}P\,\text{d}x+Q\,\text{d}y=-{∮}_{C}y\,\text{d}x.
$$
